title: steps pipeline
description: A Concourse-style pipeline with LLM agent steps. Add `# yaml-language-server: $schema=./steps.schema.json` at the top of a pipeline file for editor completion and validation.

model.description: source.model for any agent that names none.

delegate_budget_percent.description: How much of an agent's REMAINING token allowance one sub-agent call may take, pipeline-wide. Default 10. A sub-agent draws on its parent's budget rather than adding to it, so an agent's budget.tokens bounds its whole delegation subtree. Per-agent override: delegate_budget_percent on the agent.

version_history.description: How many versions of each resource steps remembers. Default 1000, or --version-history; 0 keeps everything. History is what lets a job build a version that scrolled out of a check's window, and what a passed: gate proves against — a pruned version takes its green record with it, so a number below what a slow downstream job needs will hold that job back.

run_history.description: How many runs of each job steps keeps, with their events, agent transcripts and cached step nodes. Default 100, or --run-history; 0 keeps everything. Reaping a run also drops the cached nodes no surviving run refers to, so a step whose content has not changed since before the window runs once more instead of being skipped.

preflight.description: The pre-run health check of a job's models and MCP servers. On by default.

cache.description: How long a verified target stays trusted, e.g. 5m. Keeps steps watch from probing every poll. Default 5m.

image.description: Run check/in/out in this container image instead of on the host.

env.description: Host environment variable NAMES this entity's commands may see, on top of the built-in allowlist. Names only — a KEY=VALUE literal is rejected, since a value would be hashed into the state database in cleartext.

user.description: Container user for docker's --user (e.g. "root", "1000:1000"). Empty takes the platform default: on Linux, the uid:gid running steps, so containers do not leave root-owned files in the bind-mounted working directory.

network.description: Container network for docker's --network (e.g. "none" to cut off egress entirely, "host", or a named network). Requires image: — a host-executed command uses the host's network.

privileged.description: Run the container with docker's --privileged. Requires image: — a host command already runs with whatever privileges started steps.

check.description: Prints a JSON array of version objects, oldest first.

in.description: Fetches one version into the (empty) working directory.

out.description: Publishes. Omit to make the type read-only; a put against it is then an error.

exprResourceConfig.description: Back check/in/out with expressions instead of shell commands, for a resource that is a JSON HTTP API and nothing else. Mutually exclusive with check/in/out and with mcp:. Evaluates in-process, so image:/network:/privileged:/container_limits: cannot apply.

check.description: Returns an array of version objects, oldest first. Sees source and version (the last version recorded; an empty map on the first check).

check_file.description: Path to a file holding the check expression, relative to the pipeline. Mutually exclusive with check. Suggested extension .expr.

in.description: Returns an object of artifact-relative path to file contents. Sees source, version and params. Omit to write version.json alone.

in_file.description: Path to a file holding the in expression, relative to the pipeline. Mutually exclusive with in.

out.description: Publishes, and returns the version it produced (or nil). Sees source and params, plus file() over the put's inputs.

out_file.description: Path to a file holding the out expression, relative to the pipeline. Mutually exclusive with out.

mcpResourceConfig.description: Back check/in/out with MCP tool calls instead of shell commands. Mutually exclusive with check/in/out.

args.description: The argument object sent to the tool, replacing the default payload (source for check/in, the put's params for out). String values are templates over {source, version, params}.

type.description: A resource_types: entry, or the built-in `git`.

env.description: Host environment variable NAMES this resource instance's check/in/out may see, UNIONED with its resource type's own env: (not replacing it). For when one resource of a shared type needs a credential under a different name than the type's own default.

webhook_token_env.description: Environment variable holding the shared secret a webhook must present to trigger an immediate check of this resource. The variable NAME, never the token itself.

delegate_budget_percent.description: How much of THIS agent's remaining allowance one of its sub-agent calls may take, overriding defaults.delegate_budget_percent. Never hashed, like the budget it divides.

preflight.description: Opt this agent out of (or into) the pre-run health check. For a model expected to be slow to wake.

fallback.description: Alternate sources to use, in order, when the primary model is unreachable. Selected at preflight; never affects the step's cache key.

description.description: Required when this agent is granted as a sub-agent tool.

file.description: Load this agent from a YAML document; inline fields win.

env.description: Host environment variable NAMES this entity's commands may see, on top of the built-in allowlist. Names only — a KEY=VALUE literal is rejected, since a value would be hashed into the state database in cleartext.

user.description: Container user for docker's --user (e.g. "root", "1000:1000"). Empty takes the platform default: on Linux, the uid:gid running steps, so containers do not leave root-owned files in the bind-mounted working directory.

network.description: Container network for docker's --network (e.g. "none" to cut off egress entirely, "host", or a named network). Requires image: — a host-executed command uses the host's network.

privileged.description: Run the container with docker's --privileged. Requires image: — a host command already runs with whatever privileges started steps.

system_file.description: Load system from a file, or @builtin/<name>.

max_turns.description: Tool-calling turns per attempt. Omit for the default of 30; 0 removes the cap.

timeout.description: Wall-clock deadline every step of this agent gets when it sets none of its own (e.g. "20m"). Omit for the default of 30m; "0" means no deadline. A step's own timeout: still wins.

attempts.description: How many times a step of this agent re-issues a failed request when it sets no attempts: of its own. Omit for the default of 3; 0 is rejected.

compact_after_tokens.description: Compact the conversation past this size. 0 disables.

context_window.description: This model's context window, for a model steps does not recognize or a host that serves a smaller one. Compaction fires at 80% of it.

settings.description: CLI sources only: opt the subprocess into the repo's checked-in .claude/ project scope (settings, CLAUDE.md, hooks). Absent, it loads no configuration scopes at all.

max_context_bytes.description: How much of one context_paths: file reaches the model at conversation start. Omit for the default of 100000; 0 hands the file over whole. Over the cap the file is truncated with a pointer to read_file paging, never refused.

model.description: Provider-prefixed, e.g. openai/gpt-4o or lmstudio/qwen. An @-prefixed value (e.g. "@claude/sonnet", quoted -- @ is reserved in YAML) runs a coding-agent CLI as a subprocess instead of calling an endpoint; endpoint:, the generation dials, compact_after_tokens:, budget.tokens:, and image: do not apply to one (use budget.usd: instead).

endpoint.description: Required when the model has no known provider prefix.

api_key_env.description: Environment variable holding the key. Never the key itself.

toolSpec.description: A builtin name, a custom command-backed tool, a sub-agent, or an MCP grant.

oneOf.description: A custom tool backed by a shell command.

required.description: The step cannot finish until this succeeds once.

args.description: Pinned arguments the model can neither see nor set.

oneOf.description: Expose another agent as a callable tool.
Grant tools from an mcp_servers: entry: one (tool:), a subset (tools:), or all.

endpoint.description: HTTP transport. Mutually exclusive with command.

command.description: stdio transport: a subprocess to run.

client_id.description: oauth only. A pre-registered OAuth client ID, for an authorization server that does not support dynamic client registration.

client_secret_env.description: oauth only, requires client_id. Names the environment variable holding the registered client's secret.

callback_port.description: oauth only. Pins the loopback port `steps mcp login` receives the browser redirect on, so http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback can be pre-registered with an authorization server that requires an exact redirect URI match. Defaults to an ephemeral port.

file.description: Load this task from a YAML document; inline fields win.

env.description: Host environment variable NAMES this entity's commands may see, on top of the built-in allowlist. Names only — a KEY=VALUE literal is rejected, since a value would be hashed into the state database in cleartext.

user.description: Container user for docker's --user (e.g. "root", "1000:1000"). Empty takes the platform default: on Linux, the uid:gid running steps, so containers do not leave root-owned files in the bind-mounted working directory.

network.description: Container network for docker's --network (e.g. "none" to cut off egress entirely, "host", or a named network). Requires image: — a host-executed command uses the host's network.

privileged.description: Run the container with docker's --privileged. Requires image: — a host command already runs with whatever privileges started steps.

fixSpec.description: An agent to invoke when the task's run: exits non-zero.

attempts.description: How many times the fix agent's failed request is re-issued. Omit for the agent's default; 0 is rejected, as it is on a step.

inputSpec.description: Artifact names this step reads, or the scalar `all` (put steps only).

inputSpecNames.description: Artifact names. `all` is not valid on a tasks: entry.

serial.description: State that two builds of this job must never run at once. Always true in practice — this records that a pipeline depends on it.

serial_groups.description: Locks this job holds while it runs. Two jobs sharing a group never run at the same time.

interruptible.description: If true, a steps watch shutdown cancels a running build of this job. Default false: shutdown waits for it to finish (bounded). Does not affect steps run, where ctrl-C is always immediate.

max_consecutive_failures.description: Pause this job under steps watch after this many consecutive failed triggered runs. Resume with: steps jobs resume <name>. Omit (or 0) for no circuit breaker.

timeout.description: Wall-clock deadline for the whole job, e.g. "45m". Checked BETWEEN steps: the running step finishes and no further step starts, so it composes with a step's own timeout: rather than racing it. Fails the job. Not hashed.

max_in_flight.description: Max concurrent builds of this job under steps watch. Omit (or 0) for unlimited (bounded by --max-concurrent). Rejected alongside serial:/serial_groups:, which force 1.

trigger.description: get only: poll this in `steps watch`.

version.description: get only: `latest` (default), `every`, or a pinned version object.

resource.description: get only: the resource to fetch when it differs from the step's name.

run.description: task only. Present means inline; absent means task: names a tasks: entry.

params.description: get/put only: passed to the resource command this step runs, as {{ .params.* }} — a put's reach out:, a get's reach in: (how to fetch, e.g. git depth/submodules).

attempts.description: How many times this step's work is tried. Omit for the default (1, or 3 on an agent step). 0 is rejected: unlike the other limits it does not mean unlimited, because retrying a provider that is down would never stop.

max_turns.description: Agent steps only: tool-calling turns per attempt for this one step, overriding the agent entry's max_turns. 0 removes the cap.

max_context_bytes.description: Per-file cap for this step's context_paths:, overriding the agent's max_context_bytes:. Omit to defer to the agent; 0 hands the files over whole.

try.description: Wrap a step so its failure is tolerated. The inner step's hooks and assert fire normally; to: routing sees the real outcome.

approval.description: Pause the plan until a person approves or rejects.

message.description: What is being asked. Required — an approval nobody can read is one nobody can answer responsibly.

timeout.description: How long to wait, e.g. 24h. An expired approval classifies as aborted, not failed.

load_var.description: Capture the contents of file: into a pipeline var later steps reference as ((name)).

file.description: load_var steps only: the workspace-relative file to read the value from.

passed.description: get steps only. Only run against a version that has already succeeded in every named upstream job.

across.description: Run this step once per combination of values, substituting {{ .vars.<name> }} into run/image/prompt/dir and the step's name. A values: axis expands at load; a from_file: axis expands at run time. Each cell caches independently.

from_file.description: Workspace-relative path to a JSON array of strings written by an earlier step, e.g. findings/items.json. The first path component names the artifact holding it. Mutually exclusive with values.

max_in_flight.description: across: steps only. How many cells may run at once. Unset, 0 or 1 runs them serially in declaration order. Not hashed — changing it never re-runs a cached cell.

do.description: Run several steps one after another, as a single plan step — so a hook on the block covers the whole group.

in_parallel.description: Run several steps at the same time instead of one after another.

limit.description: Maximum branches in flight at once. Omit for unbounded.

fail_fast.description: Cancel the remaining branches as soon as one fails. The block fails either way.

ensemble.description: Ask several agents the same question at once and combine their answers into one verdict to route on. Costs N times one agent.

verdicts.description: The vocabulary every member votes in, in precedence order for decide: any, and where the block's decision routes.

decide.description: majority, unanimous, any, or the name of an agent that judges.

member_errors.description: What a member that failed rather than voted does to the block. Default fail.

race.description: Run several steps at once and keep whichever finishes successfully first. A LATENCY hedge: both branches are always billed. Requires workspace isolation, and every branch must declare the same outputs.

env.description: Host environment variable NAMES this entity's commands may see, on top of the built-in allowlist. Names only — a KEY=VALUE literal is rejected, since a value would be hashed into the state database in cleartext.

user.description: Container user for docker's --user (e.g. "root", "1000:1000"). Empty takes the platform default: on Linux, the uid:gid running steps, so containers do not leave root-owned files in the bind-mounted working directory.

network.description: Container network for docker's --network (e.g. "none" to cut off egress entirely, "host", or a named network). Requires image: — a host-executed command uses the host's network.

privileged.description: Run the container with docker's --privileged. Requires image: — a host command already runs with whatever privileges started steps.

volatile.description: Never reuse this step's result. Set it on a task or agent step that reads something the pipeline never declared — a clock, a network endpoint, a path outside its inputs — where a recorded answer would be a stale one.

to.description: Route by outcome: success/failure, or a verdict name. Each value is a step name in the same get-segment, or the reserved target "next" — continue in declaration order, which is the only way to land on a container (in_parallel/race/across/ensemble/approval), since those have no name.

max_visits.description: Required when any to: target routes backward.

budget.description: across: steps only. Caps what every cell of the matrix spends TOGETHER. On exhaustion the matrix stops starting new cells and the plan continues — unlike a job or agent budget, which fails. Not hashed.

tokens.description: Provider-reported tokens the whole matrix may spend. usd is not valid here.

reserve_per_cell.description: What admission assumes an unfinished cell will spend, so tokens: binds at any max_in_flight -- without it the first max_in_flight cells are admitted against a total of ~0, and a width covering every cell bounds nothing. Omit to reserve the cell agent's own budget.tokens instead; with neither, the block admits as it did before this existed.

whenSpec.description: A guard command. Exit 0 runs the step, non-zero skips it.

contextSpec.description: What this agent or task step reads from named earlier steps of the same job.

from.description: The key is a step name, the value how much of its outcome to deliver. Demanding note or full makes that step's verdict note required.

verdicts.description: An agent's outcome vocabulary AND its routing, in one ordered list. Order is significant: it is the enum the model is offered, and an ensemble's decide: any precedence. An entry is either a bare name (record the verdict and carry on) or a single name: target pair (record it and route). failure: is the reserved catch for a step that errored or emitted nothing, and must name a target. Mutually exclusive with to:.

fileRef.description: A pipeline-relative path, or a file inside a declared input artifact.

budget.description: A ceiling on what agent work may spend. On an agent it is per invocation; on a job it is the cumulative total across every agent step. Never hashed. Use tokens: for a hosted agent and usd: for a CLI agent (@claude/...) -- each runner meters only the unit it can enforce, and the other spelling is rejected.

tokens.description: Maximum provider-reported tokens, for a hosted agent or a job. Omit budget: entirely for no ceiling; 0 is rejected.

usd.description: Maximum dollars, for a CLI agent only -- the CLI enforces it mid-conversation. Omit budget: entirely for no ceiling; 0 is rejected.

assert.description: Position decides which fields are legal: execution on a job/pipeline, outcome on a job, stdout/code/files on a task step, stdout/verdict/tool_calls/files on an agent step.

outcome.description: Job asserts only. What the plan must have CONCLUDED, as opposed to which steps ran. failed: requires an error and then clears it; succeeded: requires none, and opts out of the rule that a matching execution: clears a failure.

verdict.description: Agent steps only. The verdict the model must have emitted, matched exactly against the step's declared verdicts:.

files.description: Task/agent steps only. Every listed path must exist as a non-empty file among the step's outputs when it finishes -- checks what the step WROTE, not just what it said. Artifact-relative: the first path segment must name one of the step's outputs:.

workspace.description: Tune the per-step isolation every pipeline runs under (a step sees only its declared inputs:). Absent takes every default: strategy copy under a system temp root.

strategy.description: How step trees are materialized. Default copy; btrfs is Linux-only and requires root:.

cache.description: Reuse fetched resource versions across builds. Requires root:. Off by default: a cached version's in: does not run again, so enabling it asserts that in: is a pure fetch.

max_entries.description: How many cached versions to keep, least-recently-used evicted first. 0 takes the default.

containerLimits.description: Cap the container's CPU and memory. Requires image:. At least one of cpu/memory must be set.

cpu.description: docker --cpu-shares: a RELATIVE weight against other containers (1024 is the default), not a core count or a percentage.

memory.description: docker --memory, in bytes. A container over it is OOM-killed, which surfaces as exit code 137.
